dedupe_keys.name: libyan isp traceroute and routing data preparation workspace

description: This workspace prepares routing and cellular observations for examining internet connectivity in Libya. The maintainer publishes Python scripts and a Streamlit path analyser that parse traceroute outputs, enrich hops with GeoIP information and assemble autonomous-system relationship tables. Other scripts create cellular KML layers and process good-day and bad-day trace collections. Coverage centres on a 2025 Libyan measurement campaign; the exact sampling schedule and completeness of each output are not documented. Public code is free under MIT, while GeoLite2 databases and upstream routing or OpenCellID data have separate terms. A limitation is that public relationship inventories omit some adjacencies, and inferred paths or hidden-peering candidates are not direct observations of routing. The README describes this workspace as superseded by tracerpro despite the GitHub repository not being formally archived. Simulation uses include preparing candidate routing graphs and comparing disruption scenarios. It relates to data-opencellid as a stated cellular source. Payload traces and endpoint details were not read, crawlers were not run and no network was probed. The draft covers the preparation tools, not claiming a fully documented measurement dataset.
